findings.finding: Login brute-force protection has no per-account limiter; the only counter is keyed on client IP + email, so an attacker distributing attempts across IPs gets 5 attempts per source against a single known account
evidence: src/server/actions/contact.ts:60 — the codebase already uses an IP-independent per-email limiter for the contact form
reproduction: Inspect src/auth.ts:29 — the limiter key includes the client IP
Grep for a second rateLimit() call in the authorize() flow keyed on email alone — there is none
Compare with src/server/actions/contact.ts:60, which does key a limiter on the email alone
findings.expected: A second, IP-independent counter on the account identifier, as the contact form already does — so attempts against one account are capped regardless of source address
findings.actual: A single counter scoped to (IP, email). Each new source address resets the budget to 5 attempts per 15 minutes against the same account
findings.root_cause: The established per-identifier rate-limit pattern used elsewhere in the codebase was not applied to the login path
findings.user_impact: Credential-stuffing or password-spraying against a known admin email is materially cheaper than the 5-per-15-minutes limit implies
findings.recommendation: Add a second rateLimit() call keyed on `login:account:${hashIdentifier(email)}` with a wider window, and fail the attempt if either limiter trips. Keep the existing IP-scoped limiter for per-source throttling
regression_coverage: Proposed: assert both limiters trip independently; assert a successful login resets only the IP-scoped key

findings.finding: getClientIp() trusts the first entry of the X-Forwarded-For header, which is client-controlled unless the hosting proxy overwrites it
evidence: src/lib/rate-limit.ts:54 — const forwarded = h.get("x-forwarded-for"); if (forwarded) return forwarded.split(",")[0]!.trim();
package.json — a vercel-build script is present, suggesting Vercel, whose proxy does overwrite X-Forwarded-For
reproduction: Send a login request with a forged X-Forwarded-For header on each attempt
Observe whether the rate-limit bucket changes per forged value
findings.expected: The IP used for rate limiting is supplied by a trusted proxy and cannot be set by the client
findings.actual: Not verified at runtime. If any deployment path reaches the app without a header-normalizing proxy, the IP component of every rate-limit key becomes attacker-controlled
findings.root_cause: No trusted-proxy configuration or header allowlist; the header is read directly
findings.uncertainty: Exploitability depends entirely on the deployment topology. On Vercel the platform overwrites X-Forwarded-For and this is not exploitable. Confirm by sending a forged header to each deployed environment and checking whether the limiter bucket changes
findings.user_impact: If exploitable, every IP-scoped rate limit in the application can be bypassed at will
findings.recommendation: Document the trusted deployment topology, and prefer the platform's own IP accessor where one exists rather than parsing the header. If self-hosting is supported, read a fixed position from the right of the XFF chain based on the known proxy count
regression_coverage: Proposed: forged-XFF test asserting the limiter key is stable

findings.finding: None of the 12 API route handlers have automated test coverage, including the authorization and object-ownership checks that protect private file downloads
evidence: src/app/api/task-evidence/[id]/file/route.ts — private file download keyed by id, untested
package.json — test:unit runs six files, all under src/lib and src/server/payments; none exercise a route handler
qa/reports/evidence/mechanical/test.log — the executed suite output, confirming which tests ran
reproduction: Run npm run test:unit and note the six files executed
Grep the repository for any test referencing /api/ — there are none
findings.expected: The highest-risk code in the application — authorization and IDOR protection on private file routes — is covered by automated tests
findings.actual: Unit tests cover validation schemas, approval definitions and finance maths only. Route handlers are verified manually via the scripts/verify-*-ui.ts scripts, which are not assertions over authorization
findings.root_cause: Test strategy grew around pure functions; the HTTP boundary was never brought under test
findings.user_impact: A regression that removes an ownership check would not be caught by any gate, including CI
findings.recommendation: Add route-handler tests invoking each GET/POST directly with three actor fixtures (anonymous, authenticated non-owner, owner) and assert 401/404/200 respectively. The 404-not-403 convention already in the code makes the expected values unambiguous
regression_coverage: Proposed: one authz matrix test per route, wired into npm run check

findings.finding: A rate-limited login returns the same null result as an invalid password, so a locked-out user receives "invalid credentials" with no indication they must wait
reproduction: Submit six failed logins for the same account from one address within 15 minutes
Observe that the sixth response is indistinguishable from the fifth
findings.expected: The user learns that further attempts are temporarily blocked, with the reset time
findings.actual: Identical generic failure. A legitimate user who mistypes repeatedly will believe their password is wrong and may reset it unnecessarily
findings.root_cause: The limiter result is collapsed into the same null return as an authentication failure
findings.user_impact: Avoidable support load and unnecessary password resets; no security benefit, since the lockout is per-account-and-IP and already observable by timing
findings.recommendation: Surface a distinct, non-enumerating message such as "Too many attempts. Try again after HH:MM." The resetAt value is already returned by rateLimit()
regression_coverage: Proposed: assert the sixth attempt returns the throttled message

findings.finding: text() discards the resolved language and isFallback flag, so strings rendered through it carry no lang attribute when they fall back to the other language
evidence: src/lib/i18n/localized.ts:47 — text() returns resolve(...)?.text and drops lang and isFallback
src/components/i18n/tx.tsx:33 — the component path does set lang on fallback, showing the intended pattern
src/app/[locale]/certificates/page.tsx:48 — issuer={text(cert.issuer, locale)} renders visible text through the lossy path
reproduction: View a Tamil page where a record has no Tamil value
Inspect the rendered element for a lang attribute marking the English fallback
findings.expected: Per WCAG 3.1.2, a passage in a different language from the page carries its own lang attribute
findings.actual: Values rendered through text() inherit the page language. Most of the 48 call sites are alt text and metadata, where this is unavoidable, but a few render visible body text
findings.root_cause: Two resolution helpers with different fidelity; the lossy one is the more convenient to call
findings.user_impact: Screen readers announce fallback-language text with the wrong pronunciation rules
findings.recommendation: Audit the 48 text() call sites, and route the ones producing visible body text through the Tx component or resolve() so the lang attribute is preserved. Leave attribute and metadata uses as they are
regression_coverage: Proposed: a lint rule or test forbidding text() in visible-content positions

findings.finding: ImpactMetric.value is a Float while every monetary field in the schema correctly uses Decimal or BigInt
reproduction: Inspect the ImpactMetric model in prisma/schema.prisma
findings.expected: Published figures that may be summed or compared across periods use an exact numeric type
findings.actual: Float. Acceptable for display-only counts, but it will produce artifacts if these values are ever aggregated or compared for year-on-year equality, which the metricKey grouping comment anticipates
findings.root_cause: Display-oriented field typed before the year-on-year comparison use case was added
findings.user_impact: None today. A latent source of off-by-a-fraction display and comparison bugs
findings.recommendation: Consider Decimal if these figures will ever be aggregated. No action needed if they remain display-only — record the decision either way
